The Triceratops was a herbivorous dinosaur, which means it only ate plants. It fed
on ferns, leaves and low-growing plants from the Cretaceous period. It had a beak
similar to a parrot's that it used to cut tough plants before chewing them.

It had three horns on its face and a large bony frill behind its head. It used them
to defend itself and to show off, not to hunt, because it was not a hunter.

The Triceratops lived at the end of the Cretaceous period, about 66 million years ago,
in what is now North America. It was big: about 9 meters long and it weighed as much
as a large elephant.

It shared its time with the Tyrannosaurus Rex, which was its greatest danger. Its horns
helped it defend itself from the T-Rex.

# Leonardo da Vinci

Leonardo da Vinci was an artist and inventor from the Renaissance. He was born in 1452
in the town of Vinci, in Italy, and he died in 1519.

He painted very famous works, such as the Mona Lisa (La Gioconda) and The Last Supper.
He filled notebooks with inventions ahead of his time: flying machines, a kind of
helicopter, and even a parachute.

He loved studying nature: water, light, birds and the human body. For him, art and science
went together. He wrote many notes backwards, in mirror writing, which is read with a
mirror. He was very curious and always asked himself questions about how everything he saw

These journals are mostly written in mirror writing, also known as “reversed script,” which may have been due more to practical reasons—since this method of writing was faster—than to encryption, as has so often been suggested.
